label: Forward Kinematics
notes: Forward kinematics turns a column of joint values into one rigid-body transform of the end-effector. We frame the chapter question, name the home pose as anchor, and preview the two product-of-exponentials forms that compose individual screw motions into a single member of SE(3).

label: The Forward Kinematics Map
notes: We define the map from joint coordinates to the end-effector frame as an element of the special Euclidean group. Each joint contributes a constrained one-parameter motion, and forward kinematics asks how those motions stack to produce the observable pose of the gripper frame.

label: Screw Axes and Twists
notes: A screw axis packages an angular and a linear part into a unit twist whose matrix bracket lives in the Lie algebra se(3). Revolute joints rotate about a line; prismatic joints translate along a direction. Exponentiating the scaled twist yields the joint's rigid displacement.

label: The Matrix Exponential
notes: The matrix exponential sends a twist times its joint value to a homogeneous transform. For a revolute axis the rotation block uses Rodrigues' formula and the translation block captures the off-axis sweep. This single map converts every joint's instantaneous screw into a finite motion.

label: Home Configuration M
notes: The home configuration M records the end-effector frame relative to the fixed frame when all joint values are zero. Every product of exponentials is anchored to M; choosing it carefully removes bookkeeping and makes the screw axes easy to read straight off the mechanism drawing.

label: Space-Frame PoE
notes: The space-frame product of exponentials multiplies exponentials of the fixed-frame screw axes on the left of the home pose, ordered from the first joint outward. Each axis is expressed once in the base frame, so the formula needs only those constant space screws and M.

label: Body-Frame PoE
notes: The body-frame formula places the home pose first and multiplies exponentials of end-effector-frame screw axes on its right. It is equivalent to the space form but composes in the opposite order, convenient when the axes are most naturally described in the moving gripper frame.

label: Planar 3R Worked Example
notes: For a planar three-revolute arm every screw axis points out of the plane and the home pose places the tip at the summed link lengths. We assemble the three exponentials and read off the closed-form tip position, matching the notebook's numerical endpoint check.

label: Spatial Arm: UR5 and PUMA
notes: A six-joint spatial arm such as the UR5 or PUMA uses six space screw axes plus a home pose. We tabulate each axis from the geometry, then form the six-factor product. The same data later drives the Jacobian, so consistent screw bookkeeping pays off twice.

label: Comparison with Denavit-Hartenberg
notes: Denavit-Hartenberg parametrizes each link with four numbers tied to per-link frames, while product of exponentials needs only screw axes and one home pose. PoE avoids fragile intermediate-frame assignment and represents revolute and prismatic joints uniformly, at the cost of carrying full screw vectors.

label: Order, Pitfalls, and the URDF
notes: Joint order matters: swapping two factors changes the pose because SE(3) is non-commutative. A link-frame drawing is not a substitute for screw-axis data, and a robot description such as a URDF is reliable only when its geometry and axes genuinely agree.

label: Recap and Forward Look
notes: We recap the forward kinematics map, the two equivalent product-of-exponentials forms, the role of the home pose, and the contrast with Denavit-Hartenberg. The same screw axes that compose into the pose reappear as the columns of the Jacobian in the next chapter.
